rounds.text: Sunrest Lifescience Ltd is drastically under-appreciated by the market, trading at an exceptionally low P/E multiple of 7.93x [E1] and below book value at a price-to-book ratio of 0.80x [E2]. This disconnect is stark given the company's elite capital efficiency, boasting a robust ROCE of 28.6% [E6] and an ROE of 22.4% [E7], both of which vastly outperform broader sector medians of 12.6% for ROCE [E51] while riding a supportive healthcare sector tailwind score of +1.04 [E47]. Fundamental momentum is equally formidable, underscored by extraordinary trailing twelve-month compounded sales growth of 112% [E8] and compounded profit growth of 105% [E9]. Furthermore, operational efficiency is heading in the right direction, evidenced by debtor days dramatically improving from 282 down to 167 days [E38]. A discounted cash flow model suggests massive intrinsic undervaluation, yielding an 82% margin of safety [E24], with a reverse DCF indicating that the current market price absurdly prices in a -15.2% earnings contraction [E25] despite explosive actual growth. Conceded: cash conversion is negative at -0.01x alongside operating cash flows of -0.05 Cr in March 2026 [E14, E15], borrowings have increased to Rs 17.46 Cr [E19], and promoter holding has declined by 16.41 percentage points since March 2024 [E21].

Despite eye-catching headline growth rates, Sunrest Lifescience Ltd suffers from a severe disconnection between reported earnings and actual cash generation, highlighted by an operating cash conversion of just -0.01x and negative operating cash flows of Rs -0.05 Cr in Mar 2026 [E14, E15]. This cash crunch is severely compounded by a massive free cash flow burn of Rs -2.76 Cr alongside rising debt obligations, with total borrowings expanding from Rs 12.05 Cr to Rs 17.46 Cr over the same period [E16, E19]. Furthermore, operational efficiency remains highly suspect due to stubbornly high debtor days standing at 167, and both yearly and quarterly operating margins are explicitly flagged as inconsistent [E12, E13, E40]. Insiders are voting with their feet as promoter shareholding has plummeted by 16.41 percentage points from 69.91% in Mar 2024 to 53.50% by Jun 2026, matching a miserable 23% drop in the 1-year share price and a poor Sharpe ratio of -0.37 [E10, E21, E33]. Conceded: the company trades at a low P/E of 7.93x and an attractive price-to-book ratio of 0.80x alongside a discounted cash flow model pointing to a high theoretical margin of safety [E1, E2, E24].

Conceded: operating cash flow was negative at Rs -0.05 Cr and free cash flow burned Rs -2.76 Cr in Mar 2026 [E15, E16]. However, this cash burn is heavily offset by a massive leap in underlying operational metrics, featuring a 112% compounded sales growth and 105% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E8, E9]. Furthermore, debtor days have drastically improved from 282 down to 167 days, proving that working capital management is actively correcting [E38]. Conceded: borrowings expanded to Rs 17.46 Cr and operating margins are inconsistent [E12, E19]. Despite this, the valuation leaves an immense margin of safety because a reverse DCF shows the current price already prices in a negative 15.2% earnings growth against the 10.0% base case [E25]. Operating inside a healthcare sector enjoying a strong tailwind with a score of +1.04, the company delivers a high ROCE of 28.6% and an ROE of 22.4%, utterly dwarfing the sector medians of 12.6%, 19.1%, and 17.4% respectively [E6, E7, E48, E49, E50, E51].

Conceded: the company delivers a high ROCE of 28.6% and an ROE of 22.4%, outperforming sector medians [E6, E7, E51]. However, this reported profitability fails to translate into actual cash generation, as operating cash flow is negative at Rs -0.05 Cr and free cash flow burned Rs -2.76 Cr in Mar 2026, resulting in a disastrous cash conversion of -0.01x [E14, E15, E16]. While debtor days improved, they remain exceptionally high at 167 days, which continuously strains liquidity and forces borrowings to expand to Rs 17.46 Cr [E19, E38, E40]. Conceded: sales and profit growth over the trailing twelve months reached 112% and 105% [E8, E9]. Nevertheless, this explosive growth has entirely failed to support the share price, producing a 1-year compounded share price return of -23% and a 12-month return of -22.4%, alongside an inconsistent operating margin profile [E10, E12, E30]. Finally, the heavy insider exodus—with promoter holding plunging by 16.41 percentage points from 69.91% to 53.50%—signals a profound lack of confidence by the insiders themselves, completely undermining the theoretical margin of safety [E21, E24].
